body_markdown:
**TLDR**


- New TDS codes apply to payments from 1 April 2026, replacing section numbers under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Returns for FY 2025-26 still use the old section numbers.


- Salary TDS previously under Section 192 now falls under Section 392, with numeric codes starting from 1001.


- Non-salary TDS, including commission, rent, interest, contractor payments and professional fees, previously under the 194-series, now falls under Section 393(1).


- RazorpayX Payroll applies the new TDS codes automatically for salary and the contractor payments it supports, in payments, challans and quarterly returns, Form 138 (previously 24Q) and Form 140 (previously 26Q).


New TDS codes apply to payments from 1 April 2026, replacing the section numbers used under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Use the new codes for TDS and TCS on payments made from 1 April 2026. Returns and corrections for FY 2025-26 still use the old section numbers.


This article provides a reference of new TDS codes 2026 alongside their corresponding old section numbers, covering salary TDS, non-salary payments, special payments, and TCS across applicable resident categories.


No action required for existing RazorpayX Payroll users. The switch to the new codes is automatic, by date, with no change to your payroll setup. This article is for your information and reference only.

**What the New TDS Codes Mean for Payroll and Finance Teams**


The new TDS codes 2026 affect all TDS filings, TDS certificates, and compliance documentation that references section numbers, including the quarterly TDS returns, Form 138 (previously 24Q) and Form 140 (previously 26Q), and the annual salary TDS certificate, Form 130 (previously Form 16).


The new TDS codes most payroll teams will encounter regularly:


- **Code 1002:** salary TDS for non-government employees (old Section 192). Applies to every monthly salary TDS deduction for private sector employees.


- **Code 1023 / 1024:** contractor payments (old Section 194C). Code 1023 applies when the contractor is an individual or HUF; code 1024 when the contractor is any other entity.


- **Code 1026 / 1027:** professional and technical services (old Section 194J). Code 1026 for technical services and film royalties; code 1027 for professional services.


RazorpayX Payroll deducts and pays salary and contractor TDS every month and files the quarterly TDS returns for you.


For all other payment types, use the reference tables above to find the correct new TDS code for each category.


RazorpayX Payroll applies the new TDS codes automatically for salary and the contractor payments it supports, in payments, challans and quarterly returns, Form 138 (previously 24Q) and Form 140 (previously 26Q). It does not handle TCS. No changes are required to the existing RazorpayX payroll configuration.
